review_text: If you have Whirlpool model ED5KVEXVQ00, be aware that this ice maker requires modification to fit. There are two functional differences between this ice maker and the one that originally came in my ED5KVEXVQ00. 1. The area where the water enters the ice maker is different. On the original, the water slide enters a hole in the back of the ice maker. This part is designed to have water pour in through the top. You can, however, swap out the two pieces for water entry. It requires completely disassembling the ice maker. It's not real difficult, but if you're not willing to do this, this isn't the ice maker for you. 2. The wire bundle on the side of the ice maker is already built in to my fridge. It is easier to use the one already in the fridge. Just pop the white cover off the front of the ice maker and you will see a push tab that allows you to remove the wire bundle. You can then simply plug the existing bundle from your fridge into the new ice maker. If you're willing to make these two modifications, this ice maker fits and works well in a Whirlpool ED5KVEXVQ00 fridge.

review_text: No Holiday gathering is complete without some deviled eggs to enjoy. For years now, I have been making dozens of deviled eggs for my family, as appetizers. This set is ideal for me, as it will safely hold 4 dozen delicious deviled eggs, until I am ready to serve them. Over the years I have acquired a variety of deviled egg containers, but none were "exactly what I needed or wanted" until these ones. I've had round ones, which took up unnecessary and badly needed space in the fridge. Then there were uncovered ones that I tried to cover, as best as I could, but then I would always have to worry about the tops of my deviled eggs getting smashed. It seemed like nothing was right for the task. However, these 77L Deviled Egg Containers are FABULOUS. The lids fit securely on the rectangular (12.4" x 9.2") containers themselves, which stack neatly, one on top of the other. Only a minimum of fridge space is used: When stacked, they are only 4 inches high! You can even store one container inside the other, when not in use, to save even more space. These deviled egg holders are manufactured out of PP polypropylene plastic. It doesn't say it in the description, or even on the product, but I researched it, and polypropylene is top rack dishwasher safe. Also, I found out that polypropylene is considered to be the safest of all plastics. You may be wondering why I even bothered to research this stuff, but I was somewhat concerned about this product, because it didn't say whether or not it is BPA free. But now I can feel completely comfortable using this product, because I found out that polypropylene is one type of plastic that is indeed, BPA free. Whew! While I haven't had a chance to actually use these yet, I know that they are going to work great for my next batch of yummy deviled eggs. I am getting hungry just thinking about it! I really don't think I can wait until the holidays to have some. It's time to break with tradition, and have deviled eggs for Mother's Day, Earth Day, Flag Day, Tuesdays, Wednesdays, etc.......!!!

product_title: Whirlpool 3949238 Washer Lid Switch
review_text: It's hard to get excited about a switch. However, when my washer quit working I was happy to determine the fault was with this easy to swap out part. Much cheaper than the factory OEM part and so far it is working just fine. I considered just putting a jumper in the socket and bypassing this switch altogether but for a reasonable price this safety feature is now working as intended. **** UPDATE **** This part failed after 15 months of use. Never abused or given rough service. It just failed in the middle of a wash load. I still have the temporary jumper in my tool kit I used to keep the washer running while I waited for the replacement switch to arrive. Using that jumper again. I've ordered another switch due to the low price and Prime shipping but this will be the last. If it fails again a wire jumper across the socket and electrical tape will become my permanent solution, however I don't recommend anyone else do that. **** UPDATE # 2 **** Second switch failed in only 12 months. Will not give this supplier a third chance. Rather than just put a jumper across the socket that might come loose I cut the two wires off flush at the switch, leaving the ground wire in place. Attached the cut wires with a wire nut and sealed with electrical tape. Secured this connection up under the control panel with a cable tie. So, next time the washer isn't working I'll know it isn't due to this very poor quality switch.

product_title: Solofill V1 GOLD CUP 24K Plated Refillable Filter Cup for Coffee Pod
review_text: I've been using the Solofill V1 for close to 3 years and have loved it. Unfortunately, recently I've begun to feel that the wire mesh is getting soft when cleaning and it seems that it might be preparing to break. I decided to preemptively purchase a replacement before the old one broke since I would really hate to be without this great little refillable Vue cup. FWIW, the gold plating has been just about worn off of the old cup for ages. Upon receiving my new Solofill V1, I quickly realized the the design of the inner cup had changed. The screen area is much smaller and the holes in the screen are much smaller as well (see attached photo). I didn't think much of the difference until I tried to use new cup in my Vue. The first 2 times that I used the cup it was able to complete a full brewing cycle, however, it was only able to pump about 3/4 of of the amount of liquid through at the same setting as the old cup could. I figured that this was due to the new design so I thought that I'd offset difference by increasing the amount brewed from 12 to 14oz to see if that helped. Unfortunately, I was never able to determine if this would help, because the Vue was no longer able to complete a cycle with this new cup installed. The back pressure on the pump seemed to be quite high, and the coffee maker would simply quit in the middle of a cycle. I tried recleaning the cup, screen, etc with the same results. After 3 attempts, I gave up and did not want to make any further attempts at using this cup for fear that high pressure would damage the machine (as some other people have experienced). I can appreciate Solofill wanting to adjust their design to one that allows the coffee to steep for a longer time during the brewing process. I for one would love the stronger coffee, however, this design is simply not getting the job done. Luckily my old refillable cup is still working for now and I'll continue to use it until I can find a decent replacement. I wish I could keep the new cup but I will be contacting the vendor for a refund.
